title: Past perfect: had done
goal: Use “had done” only for the earlier of two past events
intro: The past perfect (had + past participle) shows that one past action happened before another past action: “When I reached the station, the train had left.” Many Indian speakers use “had” for any past event (“I had gone to Delhi last week”), but in English that simply sounds wrong. For a single past event, use the past simple.

rules.rule: Earlier past: had + past participle. Later past: past simple.
examples: The film had started when we arrived.
I had never seen snow before I went to Manali.

rules.rule: For one finished event, use the past simple.
examples: I went to Delhi last week.

rules.rule: With “after” and “before”, the past simple is often enough.
examples: After I finished work, I went home.

mistakes.wrong: I had gone to Delhi last week.
mistakes.right: I went to Delhi last week.
mistakes.why: Only one past event: past simple.
Only one past event: past simple.

mistakes.wrong: When I reached, the bus already left.
mistakes.right: When I reached the stop, the bus had already left.

ex.q: We ___ to the new office last month.
When I got home, everyone ___ dinner.
ex.y: Earlier than getting home: had eaten.

ex.q: I ___ never flown before that trip.
ex.y: Before a past trip: had never flown.

ex.q: Last year I had bought a new laptop.
ex.fixed: Last year I bought a new laptop.

ex.q: By the time the police came, the thief escaped.
ex.fixed: By the time the police came, the thief had escaped.
ex.y: The escape happened earlier: had escaped.

ex.q: I had spoke to him before the meeting.
ex.fixed: I had spoken to him before the meeting.

ex.q: She was upset because she ___ (lose) her wallet.

ex.a: The train had left when we reached the station.
ex.y: had + past participle for the earlier event

ex.q: Correct this: “I had met him yesterday.”

talk: Tell a story about a time you were too late for something. Say what had already happened when you arrived.
